construct.constructDefinition: Empowering Learners: self-reported digital teaching engagement/practice in the published higher-education survey. Area raw sum, not observed competence or teaching quality.

population.populationNotes: Adults teaching in higher/further education. Source study: health-sciences faculty; this separated area has no independently established administration validation. Not a school/student or validated Chinese version.

administration.timeFrame: Current practice; long-term professional goals (no fixed retrospective day window).
layoutConstraints: Keep source order and all five item-specific options. Score options in printed ascending order 0,1,2,3,4.
Prefer all six areas in original 22-item order; separated-area validity is not established.
Complete-case raw sum only. Any missing/invalid answer yields no area score; no imputation. This missingness policy is a project choice.
Do not derive global A1–C2 levels from an area or from this combination; no cross-tool total.
Estimated time is a project estimate.

intendedUses.notes: Developmental reflection on self-reported practice; area separation not independently validated.
Source study concerns higher-education health-sciences faculty, not K12 or an objectively measured performance test.

options.label: I do not create digital assignments
My students do not have problems with using digital technology
I adapt the task so as to minimize difficulties
I discuss possible obstacles with students and outline solutions
I allow for variety, e.g. I adapt the task, discuss solutions and provide alternative ways for completing the task
In my work environment, all students are required to do the same activities, irrespective of their level
I do provide students with recommendations for additional resources
I provide optional digital activities for those who are advanced or lagging behind
Whenever possible, I use digital technologies to offer differentiated learning opportunities
I systematically adapt my teaching to link to students' individual learning needs, preferences and interests
In my work environment it is not possible to actively involve students in class
I do involve students actively, but not with digital technologies
When instructing, I use motivating stimuli, e.g. videos, animations, cartoons
My students engage with digital media in my classes, e.g. electronic worksheets, games, quizzes
My students systematically use digital technologies to investigate, discuss and create knowledge

items.content: When I create digital assignments for students I consider and address potential digital problems E.g. equal access to digital devices and resources; interoperability and conversion problems; lack of digital skills
I use digital technologies to offer students personalised learning opportunities e.g. I give different students different digital tasks to address individual learning needs, preferences and interests
I use digital technologies for students to actively participate in classes

scores.label: Empowering Learners (area raw sum)
scores.description: 3 item-specific 0–4 responses summed without reversing; range 0–12. Descriptive self-report, not a validated standalone proficiency grade.

interpretations.headline: Empowering Learners: reflect on your current practice
interpretations.summary: These answers describe your own perception of practice in empowering learners. A higher raw sum means you selected options describing more digital engagement; it does not establish observed competence, student outcomes or teaching quality. Consider which practices worked for your learners and which depended on time, access or institutional support. Fewer opportunities to use technology do not make you a less capable teacher. There is no norm-based high/low category here.

guidance.text: Ask about one access barrier and offer an accessible alternative route to the same learning goal.
If access, workload or support is limiting your options, record one specific need and discuss a feasible next step with an appropriate colleague or support team.

limitations: Higher-education English survey published by Ersoy et al. (2024), dated 2023-06-02; this is not the original school Check-In, SELFIEforTEACHERS32 or a validated Chinese edition.
Area separation and this complete-case missingness policy are project adaptations. Prefer the full original 22-item sequence; no standalone area validation or norm is claimed.
Self-report is affected by opportunities, resources and interpretation. Do not use for diagnosis, performance ranking, teacher accountability or unsupported comparisons.
report.disclaimer: Teacher developmental reflection only. Missing/invalid answers mean insufficient evidence for an area score; do not substitute zero. Background and A1–C2 self-positioning forms have no calculated scores. Results remain subject to existing recipient and publication permissions.

instruction.text: Please consider where you stand in view of the following long-term goals. The answer options are organised by increasing level of engagement. Please choose the option that best reflects your current practice. This is the Empowering Learners area of the published higher-education survey. Each item has its own five options; keep their order. All area items are needed for a descriptive raw sum. Prefer the full 22-item sequence. This is developmental self-reflection, not an observed competence test.
instruction.source: First three sentences condensed from the source area instructions; remaining administration, scoring and limitation wording added by the project.
